[live-serving] the workspace logic: the answer — the statement Propositional logic evaluates formulas by assigning truth values to their atomic variables. A formula is valid when it is true on every assignment, satisfiable when it is true on at least one, and a consequence of another when it is true wherever the other is.
A follows from B when every assignment on which B is true also makes A true. Following is about the relation between formulas, not about what happens to be the case.
Modus ponens: if p implies q, and p is true, then q is true. [live-serving] the workspace photosynthesis: the answer — the statement Photosynthesis has two linked stages. The light-dependent reactions, in the thylakoid membranes, harvest light, split water and build a proton gradient that drives ATP and NADPH production. The light-independent reactions, in the chloroplast stroma, use that ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into carbohydrate through the Calvin-Benson cycle. The plant also runs cellular respiration to release that stored energy again, and it does so continuously, including in daylight.
Cellular respiration is the process by which cells break down glucose to release energy.
Cellular respiration is a set of reactions in which the energy in nutrients is transferred to ATP by moving electrons to an inorganic electron acceptor, typically oxygen, and releasing waste products. It runs continuously in plant cells, including during daylight, so a plant both makes sugar by photosynthesis and spends it by respiration.
Photorespiration is a wasteful side reaction of photosynthesis: the plant's main carbon-fixing enzyme grabs oxygen instead of carbon dioxide, and the plant has to spend energy undoing the result.
Oxidative phosphorylation is the third stage of cellular respiration.
The Krebs cycle is the second stage of cellular respiration.
Glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration.
Stomata are adjustable pores in the leaf through which carbon dioxide enters and water vapour leaves. Stomatal conductance measures how freely gas moves through them. It responds to light, to the carbon dioxide concentration and to the plant's water supply, so closing the stomata to conserve water also restricts the carbon dioxide supply for photosynthesis.
The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membrane. Light-harvesting complex II transfers excitation energy to the photosystem II core, which extracts electrons from water; the electrons pass through the electron transport chain, protons are moved into the thylakoid lumen, and the gradient drives ATP synthase. The system must also dissipate excess excitation as heat, because unbalanced absorption produces damaging reactive oxygen species. Activation of RuBisCO lags when a shaded leaf is suddenly exposed to strong light, and that lag alone has been estimated to cut wheat assimilation by about a fifth.
RuBisCO is the enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide, adding it to a five-carbon sugar to start the Calvin-Benson cycle.
